analysis.title: Prime Insights and Analytics Chart Pack - Asia
key_insights: Asia-focused Fundamental L/S hedge funds are down 8.9% MTD in October versus MXAP -6.4%, as the AI sell-off accelerated. The drawdown came from beta, asset selection alpha, and the Momentum and Volatility factors.
Asia Fundamental L/S YTD performance is 14.5% on a weighted-average basis, but the simple average is 9.3% and the median is 2.7%, so dispersion across managers is elevated.
China-focused Fundamental L/S managers are down 10.9% MTD (YTD 16.8%). Both MTD and YTD returns are driven by AI-related investments outside China.
Japan-focused managers are down 1.9% MTD (YTD 10.7%). Global Fundamental L/S is down 3.8% MTD (+8.8% YTD). Global Systematics is down 1.1% MTD (+18.7% YTD).
The Global Prime book saw large net selling MTD, with short sales well above long sales. North America and Asia dominated the selling.
Asian equities saw heavy net selling as the AI sell-off accelerated, with short sales exceeding long sales 1.7 to 1. Emerging Markets dominated the selling versus Developed Markets.
Taiwan, Korea and Japan led the selling MTD, with a smaller contribution from China, as hedge funds unwind AI exposures. Risk-on flows in Japan and China were offset by de-grossing in Korea.
Japan was net sold MTD, mostly through short sales in single stocks. Net allocation fell sharply while gross allocation fell less.
China saw moderate net selling, with short sales dominating long buys. A-shares led the net selling and the risk-on flows. US ADRs also added to net selling, while H-shares saw risk-on activity.

Net allocation to Asia in the Global Prime book fell 289 bps MTD to 27.3%, a 10.9% overweight versus the MSCI World benchmark. That compares with a 20% overweight in mid-June and a 10.9% low on 30 July.
Gross allocation to Asia fell 135 bps to 24.5%, an 8.0% overweight relative to MSCI World.
6 of 11 sectors were net sold MTD. Info Tech led the selling, followed by Financials, Communication Services and Industrials. Health Care was the most net bought, followed by Materials and Energy.
Info Tech remains 14.2% overweight versus MXAP, down from a ~22% peak in June and above the 11% overweight at the start of the year. Taiwan and Korea dominated the sector's net selling.
Korea continues to dominate net selling and de-grossing in the region, mostly through long sales. Net allocation fell to 3.4% (peak ~8% in June, 2.5% at the start of the year).
Taiwan saw large selling MTD, split equally between long and short sales. Net allocation fell to 6.4% and gross allocation is 4.3%, both in high 5-year percentiles.

sector_views.rationale: Info Tech led net selling MTD, mainly in Taiwan and Korea, though hedge funds remain 14.2% overweight versus MXAP.
Health Care was the most net bought Asian sector MTD, followed by Materials and Energy. This is a flow observation, not a stated view.

risk_factors: The AI sell-off is accelerating and hedge funds are unwinding AI exposures across Taiwan, Korea and Japan.
Manager dispersion is elevated, with a median Asia Fundamental L/S YTD return of 2.7% against a weighted average of 14.5%.
Asia allocations remain significantly overweight versus the MSCI World benchmark, leaving room for further reduction.
vol_and_positioning: Asia net allocation in the Global Prime book is 27.3%, a 10.9% overweight versus MSCI World, down 289 bps MTD. Gross allocation is 24.5%, an 8.0% overweight, down 135 bps.
Korea net allocation is 3.4% (29th percentile 1-year, 86th percentile 5-year). Korea gross allocation is 2.4% (30th percentile 1-year, 86th percentile 5-year).
Taiwan net allocation is 6.4% (56th percentile 1-year, 91st percentile 5-year). Taiwan gross allocation is 4.3% (74th percentile 1-year, 95th percentile 5-year).
Short sales exceeded long sales 1.7 to 1 in Asian equities MTD, with hedge funds de-grossing in Korea.
